why: NOTES-FROM-PLANNING.md entry 150 section 1. Alan, reading the releases page: a lot of builds are
extremely minor, release note pages brought up to date or research articles written, and every one
of them compiled and tested a new executable. Nightly 84 was all website changes.
So: a new executable exists only when something that ships inside the executable changed. Everything
else is content, and content publishes through the site path entry 144 built.
Both the nightly workflow and a test read this file, so the gate and the rule cannot drift apart.
A path in neither list is a failure rather than a default, because a new top level directory should
make somebody decide which side it is on instead of silently picking one.
rule: The first segment of a changed path decides. A top level file is its own entry.

ships..gitattributes: line endings at checkout, and a test has already failed over CRLF on a Windows runner
ships..github: the build, packaging and release workflows themselves, and this file
ships.Directory.Build.props: the version the build is named from, and the compiler settings
ships.reference: ballistics reference data the tests measure against, so a change here can fail the build
ships.samples: sample sheets the tests decode, so a change here can fail the build
ships.scans: the real scans the detection tests run against
ships.scripts: the build and release scripts, including the release notes generator
ships.targets: target definitions embedded in the application, not only printed by the site
ships.tests: the tests, where a failure stops the build
ships.tools: the reference encoder the fixtures are dumped from

content.CLAUDE.md: the rules this session works to, read by nobody at runtime
content.README.md: documentation, and the site reads it
content.docs: documentation, the release notes, the guides and the research articles
